elements.id-string-7: The emergence of chiral anomaly entails various fascinating phenomena such as anomalous quantum Hall effect and chiral magnetic effect in different branches of (non-)Hermitian physics.
elements.id-string-8: While in the single-particle picture, anomalous currents merely appear due to the coupling of massless particles with background fields, many-body interactions can also be responsible for anomalous transport in interacting systems.
elements.id-string-9: In this Letter, we study anomalous chiral currents in systems where interacting massless fermions with complex Fermi velocities are coupled to complex gauge fields.
elements.id-string-10: Our results reveal that incorporating non-Hermiticity and many-body interactions gives rise to additional terms in anomalous relations beyond their Hermitian counterparts.
elements.id-string-11: We further present that many-body corrections in the subsequent non-Hermitian chiral magnetic field or anomalous Hall effect are nonvanishing in nonequilibrium or inhomogeneous systems.Our results advance efforts in understanding the anomalous transport in interacting non-Hermitian systems.
elements.id-string-14: The chiral anomaly emerges due to the violation of classical chiral symmetry by quantum fluctuations in odd spatial dimensions.
elements.id-string-15: This quantum anomaly has given rise to a plethora of exotic phenomena, including anomalous decay of neutral pion in high-energy physics~\cite{Bell1969, Adler1969, Adler1969b, Bilal2008, Zinn2019}, anomaly-induced charges in baryons in quantum chromodynamics~\cite{Eto2012}, anomalous transport in condensed matter physics~\cite{Zyuzin2012, Hosur2013, Landsteiner2016, Frohlich2018, Araki2019, Arouca2022, Frohlich2023}, and the magnetic helicity transfer in the early universe due to chiral asymmetry in cosmology~\cite{Boyarsky2012, Brandenburg2017}.
elements.id-string-16: Aside from deepening our understanding and their experimental realizations~\cite{Huang2015, Hirschberger2016, Zhang2016, Li2016, Ong2021}, chiral anomalies are proposed to be used in advancing quantum computing, e.g., as chiral qubits~\cite{Kharzeev2019, Babaev2023}.

elements.id-string-30: Addressing the anomalous chiral response of interacting Dirac fermions in non-Hermitian models is the primary goal of this work.
elements.id-string-31: In this letter, we explore the chiral anomaly in $(1+1)$ and $(3+1)$ dimensions for non-Hermitian Dirac fermions with complex Fermi velocities coupled to complex background gauge fields.
elements.id-string-32: By introducing a unified notation, we bring the non-Hermitian model and its symmetrized version under the same umbrella, enabling us to identify purely non-Hermitian contributions in anomalous currents.
elements.id-string-33: We further present the physical consequences of the non-Hermitian chiral anomaly in non-Hermitian systems and discuss plausible platforms to realize them.

elements.id-string-140: In conclusion, we have presented how non-Hermitian chiral anomalies for massless fermions with complex Fermi velocities coupled to complex background fields are modified in the presence of four-particle interactions.
elements.id-string-141: We have shown that anomalous relations cast the same form as the chiral anomaly in Hermitian (non)interacting systems.
elements.id-string-142: Despite the similar structure, the embedded terms in the presented non-Hermitian chiral anomaly exceed those in the Hermitionized model.
elements.id-string-143: Our results show that nonperturbative interaction corrections to chiral anomalies are nonvanishing in nonequilibrium or inhomogeneous systems.
elements.id-string-144: This can be seen in the presented non-Hermitian chiral magnetic effect and non-Hermitian anomalous Hall effect.
